lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
- Cut the booking flow's JavaScript from 410 KB to 260 KB by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Moving image resizing to the CDN, inlining critical CSS, preloading the two web fonts and deferring the analytics script, raised the checkout page's Lighthouse performance score from 52 to 91.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Documented the design-system tokens in Storybook so designers could check spacing and color values without asking engineers.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Apr 2024 - Aug 2024
- Cut the university sites' JavaScript bundle by 60% by converting their PNG images to WebP.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Writes the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cut cold-start time on slow 3G from 3.0s to 1.5s, a 75% improvement, by caching the stop list offline.
- Raised weekly returning riders by 10% in the first month, from 30% to 40%, by adding saved stops.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Presented the demo to the library staff and handed over the code with setup notes.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The portfolio address looks like a placeholder rather than a working, clickable link to relevant work.
Date formatting should be consistent across the experience and project entries.
items.because: The education dates use a clear style.

items.says: The 9% booking increase does not say whether it is relative or in percentage points.
items.because: The business result would be easier to interpret.

items.says: The A/B test lacks context such as duration or sample size.
items.because: Test context would make the result easier to assess.

items.says: The JavaScript sizes do not say whether they are compressed or uncompressed.
items.because: Readers may not be able to compare the before-and-after numbers.

items.says: The audit standard or type is not named.
items.because: It is unclear what the 14 issues refer to.

items.says: The bullet does not indicate whether the accessibility fixes were verified.
items.because: “All 14” is a strong claim.

items.says: The verb construction should read grammatically and match the other past-tense bullets.
The Lighthouse test conditions are unclear.
items.because: Scores can vary with device and test setup.

items.says: The claim that lazy-loading the hero image caused the LCP improvement needs checking.
items.because: Hero images are usually visible immediately, and lazy-loading can delay LCP.

items.says: The before-and-after LCP measurement should be verified.
The Storybook bullet is less outcome-focused than the other bullets.
items.because: Its benefit or scope could be clearer.

items.says: Converting PNGs to WebP does not generally reduce the JavaScript bundle.
items.because: It generally reduces image or page payload instead.

items.says: Your own contribution to the preview mode is unclear.
items.because: Clarifying it would make the connection between your work and the outcome more credible.

items.says: The period over which broken-page reports fell is unclear.
items.because: Clarifying it would make the connection between your work and the outcome more credible.

items.says: “Writes” uses present tense for a role that ended in August 2024.
items.because: The tense should match the rest of the completed role.

items.says: The bullet does not explain what “failed audits” counts or over what period.
“Search time” does not say what was measured or how it was tested.
items.because: This would distinguish a user-facing improvement from a technical timing metric.

items.says: The weekly rider count does not say how it was measured.
items.because: Readers should be able to assess or verify the usage claim.

items.says: The project lacks a project or live-app link, if one is available.
items.because: Readers should be able to assess or verify its scale.

items.says: The distinction between completed work and current usage could be clearer.
items.because: The project is ongoing.

items.says: A change from 3.0 seconds to 1.5 seconds is a 50% reduction, not a 75% improvement.
It is unclear whether “cold-start” accurately describes what was measured.
It is unclear whether caching the stop list explains the improvement.
A change from 30% to 40% is 10 percentage points, not a 10% relative increase.
The measurement period and user sample for returning riders are unclear.
The heading lists Vue, while the first bullet says the frontend used React and TypeScript.
items.because: The listed technologies should match the work described.

items.says: The broad frontend statement overlaps with the calendar-component bullet.
items.because: It does not make your individual ownership or distinct contribution clear.

items.says: The type or scope of the calendar tests is unspecified.
items.because: Readers cannot tell how thoroughly the edge cases were covered.

items.says: The demo and handoff are a weaker result than the implementation bullets.
items.because: Their importance or concrete outcome is not clear.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
The “Tools” list mixes a programming language, frameworks, and a documentation tool.
items.because: The grouping should reflect what each item is.

items.says: Angular does not appear elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: Keep it only if you can comfortably discuss your experience with it.

items.says: The skills list omits JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and a specific testing tool.
items.because: Specificity is more useful than a long, generic list.
